findings.message: The compound `(.result_contract == 2) and has("test_output")` is still tautological: the acceptance gate confirms NEGCTL FAIL for SPEC-1 because the baseline artifact already satisfies both sub-conditions simultaneously, so the assertion passes at v1 baseline and provides no regression guard for the field-presence change.

Same tautology as SPEC-1: `(.result_contract == 2) and has("run_mode")` evaluates to true at v1 baseline (NEGCTL FAIL SPEC-2), meaning adding the result_contract guard does not make the assertion discriminate pre-fix from post-fix output.

SPEC-8 replaces `has("test_output")` with `.result_contract == 2`, which is already asserted by SPEC-1 on the same artifact (`OUT_JSON_3`); the second half of the pipe-joined assertion now duplicates SPEC-1's check rather than testing an independent property (top-level test_output on the interrupted signal path), leaving that specific condition unguarded.

The compound `(.result_contract == 2) and has("test_output")` is tautological at v1 baseline (NEGCTL FAIL SPEC-11); the change makes the same logical error as SPEC-1/2/5/6 — both sub-conditions are already true in the baseline artifact, so the conjunction is always true regardless of whether the fix is applied.

The compound `(.result_contract == 2) and (.run_mode == "full")` is tautological at v1 baseline (NEGCTL FAIL SPEC-11); if the fallback writer already emits result_contract=2 and run_mode at top level before this change, the assertion cannot detect a regression where those fields are absent.

SPEC-5 uses the same compound guard `(.result_contract == 2) and has("test_output")` against `OUT_JSON_2` (error/missing-diff path); if the baseline error-path artifact also already has result_contract=2 and test_output at top level, this assertion is equally tautological and the acceptance gate confirms it (NEGCTL FAIL SPEC-5).

SPEC-1, SPEC-2, SPEC-5, SPEC-6, and SPEC-8 each still spawn a separate jq subprocess on the same already-parsed JSON file where a single jq call could extract result_contract and all required fields in one pass; the diff folds extra boolean logic into each individual invocation rather than consolidating them, leaving ~5 avoidable forks in the test run.

Adding `(.result_contract == 2) and` does not fix a tautology when the baseline artifact already emits result_contract:2 — both halves of the `and` are true at baseline, so NEGCTL still passes; the acceptance-gate confirms all nine SPEC assertions (SPEC-1/2/5/6/7/8/11) remain tautological after this change.

SPEC-7 is explicitly listed as tautological by the acceptance-gate but is not touched in this diff — it still uses bare `has('exit_code')` without any result_contract guard, so it passes on a v1 result that happens to expose exit_code at top level.

SPEC-8 pipe-delimits `_spec8_term` (signal-death mapping) with `_spec8_rc2` (jq boolean from OUT_JSON_3); if jq fails or OUT_JSON_3 is absent, `_spec8_rc2` silently collapses to empty string via `2>/dev/null`, producing composite `'interrupted|'` that matches nothing rather than failing with a clear diagnostic.

The combined jq boolean `(.result_contract == 2) and has('field')` returns a single true/false that cannot distinguish 'wrong contract version' from 'required field absent', so any assertion failure is opaque about which invariant broke.

SPEC-11 in the fallback-writer test now asserts `(.result_contract == 2) and (.run_mode == 'full')`; if the baseline implementation already writes result_contract:2 and run_mode:full (consistent with the acceptance-gate NEGCTL FAIL), this assertion is also tautological and does not guard the v2 contract shape it claims to verify.

SPEC-3, SPEC-4, and SPEC-7 are flagged as tautological by the acceptance-gate (same iteration, listed alongside SPEC-1/2/5/6/8/11) but this diff does not touch those assertions — they remain unaddressed despite being part of the same tautology class the plan aims to fix.

Scope manifest is still inaccessible (permission denied), so out-of-scope edits and the full declared file list cannot be verified against the diff; findings here are limited to what the diff and stage summaries reveal.

The pipe-delimited compound assertion `"interrupted|true"` vs `"${_spec8_term}|${_spec8_rc2}"` could silently pass if either variable contains a literal pipe character, but `_spec8_rc2` is now sourced from `jq '.result_contract == 2'` which can only emit `true` or `false`, and `_spec8_term` comes from an internal mapping function — practical risk remains negligible and is lower than before this change.

The acceptance-gate confirms SPEC-1/2/5/6/8/11 are still tautological after this change: the baseline artifact already satisfies `(.result_contract == 2) and has("test_output")`, so a regression that drops result_contract back to v1 or removes top-level fields will still pass these guards, leaving the production schema contract undetected.

SPEC-11 integration guard has the same tautology: if the baseline artifact already carries result_contract=2, the compound jq expression is satisfied regardless of whether the implementation change is present, removing the regression signal for v2 schema shape on the summary-format path.

SPEC-11 unit guard now asserts `(.result_contract == 2) and (.run_mode == "full")` but the acceptance-gate reports it is still tautological, meaning a writer regression that omits result_contract or emits v1 shape will not be caught by this suite.

SPEC-8 still concatenates two unrelated checks into a single string (`"interrupted|true"`); when the assertion fires on-call, the failure message provides no indication of which sub-check (signal mapping or contract version) failed, slowing incident diagnosis.

No assertion verifies that top-level exit_code and data.exit_code carry the same value; if a code path updates one but not the other, downstream consumers reading different paths will silently diverge with no test signal (gap persists from prior change).
